79:1: Interpretation of Surat An-Nazi'at In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn Abbas, Masruq, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, Abu Ad-Dhaha, and As-Suddi said: “And the angels who pull out the souls of the sons of Adam, meaning when they pull out the souls of some of them with difficulty, so they drown in its removal, and the souls of some of them are taken easily, as if they were released from the fire. This is His statement: “And the angels who pull out energetically,” as said by Ibn Abbas. From Ibn Abbas: And the angels who pull out are the souls of the disbelievers, they are pulled out, then revived, then drowned in the fire. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Mujahid said: And the angels who pull out energetically means death. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: And the angels who pull out energetically are the stars. Ata` ibn Abi Rabah said about His statement: And the angels who pull out “And the angels who pull out” are the bows in battle. The first is correct, and most agree with it. As for the Almighty’s saying: And those that swim in glory, Ibn Masoud said: They are the angels. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ali, Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubair, and Abu Salih. And on the authority of Mujahid: And those that swim in glory means death. Qatada said: They are the stars. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: They are the ships. God the Almighty said: And those who race in race It was narrated on the authority of Ali, Masruq, Mujahid, Abu Salih and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, meaning the angels. Al-Hasan said: They raced to faith and belief in it. Mujahid said: Death. Qatadah said: They are the stars. Ata' said: They are the horses in the way of God. God the Almighty said: And those who manage an affair Ali, Mujahid, Ata', Abu Salih, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Rabi' bin Anas and Al-Suddi said: They are the angels. Al-Hasan added: They manage the affair from the heaven to the earth, meaning by the command of their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. They did not differ on this, and Ibn Jarir did not definitively mean any of that, except that he narrated that those who manage an affair are the angels, and he neither affirmed nor denied. And the Almighty said: The Day the Earthquake shakes, followed by the second. Ibn Abbas said: They are the first and second blasts. This is what Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and others said. And from Mujahid: As for the first, which is His Almighty’s statement: The Day the Earthquake shakes, it is like His statement, may His Majesty be glorified: The Day the earth and the mountains shake. And the second, which is the second blast, is like His statement: And the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single blow. Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqeel, on the authority of At-Tufayl bin Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Earthquake has come, followed by the second blast. Death has come with what it contains. A man said: O Messenger of God, what if I make all my prayers upon you? He said: Then God will suffice you in what concerns you of your world and your hereafter.” At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Sufyan Ath-Thawri with a similar chain of transmission. The wording of At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Abi Hatim was: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When two-thirds of the night had passed, he would stand up and say: “O people, remember God. The first earthquake has come, followed by the second. Death has come with what it contains.” God the Almighty says: {Hearts that Day will be trembling.} Ibn Abbas said: meaning fearful. Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. Their eyes will be humbled. That is, the eyes of their owners. It is only attributed to them for connection, meaning humiliated and contemptible because of what they witnessed of horrors. God the Almighty says: {They will say, Shall we then be returned to the grave?} meaning the polytheists of Quraysh and those who share their saying in denying the Resurrection. They rule out the occurrence of resurrection after being destined for the grave, which is the graves, as Mujahid said, and after their bodies have been torn apart and their bones have crumbled and decayed. For this reason they said: {Shall we then be rotten bones?” It was read as rotten. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: meaning worn out. Ibn Abbas said: It is a bone when it has decayed and the wind has entered it. They will say, “That then will be a losing return.} It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Ikrimah, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Abu Malik, As-Suddi and Qatadah: The grave is life after death. Ibn Zayd said: The grave is Hell. How many are its names! They are Fire, Hellfire, Saqar, Jahannam, Al-Hawiyah, Al-Haferah, Al-Laza, and Al-Hutmah. As for their saying, That then is a losing ball, Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Quraysh said, If God revives us after we die, we will surely lose. God the Most High said, “It will be only a single blast. Then at once they will be at the Watcher.” That is, it is only a command from God, with no duality or emphasis in it. Then the people will stand and watch, and that is when God the Most High will command Israfil to blow the Trumpet of Resurrection. Then the first and the last will stand before the Lord Almighty, watching, as God the Most High said, Our command is but one, like the twinkling of an eye. And He the Most High said, And the matter of the Hour is not but like the twinkling of an eye, or even nearer. Mujahid said: It will be only one blast, one shout. Ibrahim At-Taymi said: The most angry the Lord will be with His creation on the Day He resurrects them. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A blast of wrath. Abu Malik and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: A single blast is the last trumpet blast. God the Almighty said: Then behold, they are about to attack the Sahira, Ibn Abbas said: The Sahira is the entire earth. Sa’id bin Jubayr, Qatadah and Abu Salih said the same. Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: The Sahira is the face of the earth. Mujahid said: They were at its lowest point then they were brought out to its highest point. He said: The Sahira is the level place. Ath-Thawri said: The Sahira is the land of Ash-Sham. Uthman bin Abi Al-Atika said: The Sahira is the land of Jerusalem. Wahb bin Munabbih said: The Sahira is a mountain next to Jerusalem. Qatadah also said: The Sahira is Hell. All of these are strange statements, but the correct view is that it is the upper surface of the earth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Hazr bin Al-Mubarak, the righteous sheikh, told us, Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us, Mus`ab bin Thabit told us, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Sahl bin Sa`d Al-Sa`idi, Then behold, they are upon the plain, he said: A white, dusty, empty land like pure bread. Al-Rabi` bin Anas said: Then behold, they are upon the plain, God the Almighty says: The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], and they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing. And God the Almighty says: “And they ask you about the mountains. Say, ‘My Lord will blow them away with a blast.’ He will leave them as a level plain. You will see therein neither crookedness nor unevenness.” And God the Almighty says: And the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth appearing, and the earth on which the mountains are will emerge, and it is not counted as part of this earth, and it is a land on which no sin has been committed and on which no blood has been shed.

79:15: God Almighty informs His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, about His servant and messenger Moses, peace be upon him, that He sent him to Pharaoh, and God supported him with miracles, and despite this, he continued in his disbelief and tyranny until God seized him with the grip of the Mighty, the Powerful. And this is the end of the one who opposes you and denies what you have brought. That is why He said at the end of the story: Indeed in that is a lesson for him who fears. So God Almighty says: Has there come to you the story of Moses? That is, have you heard his story when his Lord called to him That is, He spoke to him with a call in the sacred valley That is, the purified Tuwa That is, the name of the valley according to the correct view as mentioned previously in Surat Taha, and He said to him: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed That is, he has become tyrannical, rebellious, and insolent. And say, ‘Would you like to be purified?’ That is, say to him, Would you like to respond to a method and conduct by which you will be purified and submit and obey? “And I will guide you to your Lord That is, I will direct you to the worship of your Lord so that you may fear That is, so that your heart will become submissive and obedient to Him. So he showed him the greatest sign, meaning that Moses showed him, along with this true call, a strong argument and clear proof of the truth of what he had brought from God. But he denied and disobeyed, meaning that he denied the truth and disobeyed what he had been commanded to do in terms of obedience. The gist of it is that he disbelieved in his heart, so he was not affected by Moses inwardly or outwardly. His knowledge that what he had brought was true does not necessarily mean that he believed in it, because knowledge is the knowledge of the heart and faith is its action, which is submission to the truth and humility to it. And the Almighty’s saying: Then he turned back, striving meaning to confront truth with falsehood, and he gathered the magicians to confront the dazzling miracles that Moses, peace be upon him, had brought. So he was gathered and called out meaning to his people, and said, ‘I am your most high lord.’ Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: This statement was uttered by Pharaoh forty years after he had said, I do not know of any god for you other than me. God Almighty said: So God seized him as a punishment for the Hereafter and for the first time meaning God took revenge on him with a punishment that made him an example and a punishment for his rebellious peers in this world. And on the Day of Resurrection, wretched is the provision as God Almighty said: And We made them leaders inviting to the Fire, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided. This is the correct meaning of the verse, that what is meant by His saying: The punishment for the Hereafter and the first time means this world and the Hereafter. It was said that what is meant by this is his first and second statements, and it was said that it refers to his disbelief and disobedience, but the correct and undoubted opinion is the first. And His saying: Indeed in that is a lesson for whoever fears means for whoever takes heed and is warned.

79:27: God Almighty says, arguing with those who deny the resurrection regarding the re-creation after its beginning: Are you O people more difficult to create, or is the heaven? meaning, the heaven is more difficult to create than you, as God Almighty says: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind. And God Almighty says: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. And God Almighty’s statement: He constructed it is explained by His statement: He raised its ceiling and proportioned it. That is, He made it a high structure, far from perishable, level in its regions, and crowned with stars in the dark night. And God Almighty says: And He covered its night and brought forth its brightness, that is, He made its night dark and pitch black, and its day bright, radiant, luminous, and clear. Ibn Abbas said: He covered its night, meaning He made it dark. Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, and many others said the same. And brought forth its brightness, meaning He illuminated its day. And the Almighty’s saying: And the earth, after that, He spread it out is explained by His saying: He brought forth from it its water and its pasture. It was mentioned previously in Surah Ha Mim As-Sajdah that the earth was created before the creation of the heaven, but it was only spread out after the creation of the heaven, meaning that He brought forth what was in it potentially into action. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas and others, and it was chosen by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Ja’far Ar-Raqi told us, Ubaidullah told us, meaning Ibn Amr, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, on the authority of Al-Minhal bin Amr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, He spread it out. And He spread it out means He brought forth from it water and pasture, and split rivers in it, and made in it mountains, sand, paths, and hills. So that is His saying: And the earth, after that, He spread it out. And the explanation of that was mentioned previously there. God Almighty says: And the mountains He has fixed firmly meaning He has established them, made them firm, and confirmed them in their places. He is the Wise, the All-Knowing, the Compassionate, the Merciful to His creation. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God created the earth, it began to shake, so He created the mountains and placed them on it until it settled. The angels were amazed at the creation of the mountains and said: ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is harder than mountains?’ He said: ‘Yes, iron.’ They said: ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is harder than iron?’ He said: ‘Yes, fire.’ They said: ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is harder than fire?’ He said: ‘Yes, water.’ They said: ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is harder than water?’ He said: ‘Yes, the wind.’ They said: ‘O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is harder than the wind?’ He said: ‘Yes, the son of Adam gives charity with his right hand, hiding it from his left.’” Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of Ali, who said: When God created the earth, it shuddered and said: ‘They will create upon Adam and his offspring, who will throw their stench upon me and accuse me of sins.’ So God anchored it with mountains, some of which you see and some of which you do not see.’ You do not see, and the first settlement of the earth was like the meat of a camel when it is slaughtered, its meat throbs. Very strange. And the Almighty’s saying: For provision for you and your livestock, meaning He spread out the earth, so its springs gush forth, and revealed its hidden things, and made its rivers flow, and caused its crops, trees and fruits to grow. And He made its mountains firm so that its people would settle and its settlement would be secure. As for evening, it is what is between noon and sunset, {or a morning thereof}, what is between sunrise and noon. Qatada said: The time of this world in the eyes of the people is when they witness the Hereafter. End of the interpretation of Surat An-Nazi’at. Praise and thanks be to God.

Ibn Abbas said that it was called that because it overshadows every terrible and horrific matter, as God Almighty said: And the Hour is more terrible and bitter. “The Day when man will remember what he strove for,” meaning that then the son of Adam will remember all of his deeds, both good and bad, as God Almighty said: On that Day man will remember, but how will remembrance succeed him? “And Hellfire will be made visible to all who see,” meaning that it will be made visible to onlookers, so people will see it clearly. But as for he who transgressed, meaning that he rebelled and acted insolently, and preferred the life of this world, meaning that he preferred it over his religious and afterlife matters, then indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge, meaning that his destination will be Hellfire, and his food will be from Zaqqum and his drink from scalding water. But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from inclination, meaning that he feared standing before God Almighty and feared God’s judgment regarding him and prevented himself from his inclinations and returned it to the obedience of its Master, then indeed, Paradise will be the refuge, meaning his place of return, destination, and return to Paradise.
